surfaces.part: stair tread 1 (top step, inside the arch)

answer.evidence: The main body is a descending staircase. Each step has a tread band 3-4 rows tall that ends in a light front-edge line (rows 11, 17, 25, 34, 43). Each edge line is followed by 1-3 rows of dark shadow and then a riser of 2-3 rows. This repeats down the image and gives a stepped three-quarter read. The stone frame at the top is a thin front-facing strip, and the side walls are vertical faces, which is normal for the south view. The treads show clear top surfaces with edge lines and shadows, so this is not a flat front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a stone archway with wooden stairs descending into a dark recess. Its 11 visible tones per tile sit between the two references (15 and 7). Near-flat coverage is 8%, close to the window wall (9%) and well below any flat-fill concern. The stair treads show about 4-5 wood steps with highlight edges and the stone arch has a few tone steps, so shading depth is comparable to the references. The dark edge pixels are only 14% neutral, so the outlines lean brown or blue-grey and follow the adjacent material. The references are 100% neutral, so the candidate is not the sticker look. Texture is moderate: stair grain and stone block lines are present, but there is less speckle and per-stone shading than the door reference. The overall look is slightly simpler than castle-door2-closed, but it is a fair match for the window wall and would sit acceptably beside both.
